A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Llamdex research despite the revised title and organization. Text, equations, tables, and figures are readable and support comparison. v1 ends with references and has no appendix; v2 includes complete Appendices A–E.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on four tabular datasets, including accuracy, privacy–utility curves, insertion-layer sensitivity, and training and inference resource measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds privacy-baseline comparisons, Adult results, F1 scores, Llama-2 experiments, component ablations, and a reasoning example.

M1.justification: Section 5.3 adds optional feedback inference: an answer-augmented question is resubmitted to the original LLM for explanations. The core architecture, token mapping, losses, and separate encoder/decoder training remain unchanged. The rewritten introduction does not establish a different core training algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 retains Titanic, Wine, Bank, and Nursery and adds Adult classification in Appendix C, Table 8. Table 6 also adds a follow-up explanation scenario using a Titanic example. Coverage expands modestly within the existing tabular-domain setting.

E2.justification: The central privacy comparison expands from PATE-GAN as the sole data-synthesis baseline to include evaluated SeqPATE and PromptPATE curves in Figure 4. Original LLM, PATE-GAN, and the API comparator, labeled Prompt API in the plots, remain present. This substantially broadens the evidence against alternative privacy-preserving approaches.

E3.justification: v2 substantially expands evaluation design through F1 scoring, a Llama-2-7B comparison, and controlled variations of token mapping, padding, and expert-output weight. The token-count experiment tests 1, 5, 10, and 20 output tokens at insertion layer 0. Existing 80/20 splits, 10% masking, and stated training budgets are retained.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's insertion-depth analysis, Appendix D adds tests of base-LLM robustness, output-token count, token-mapping removal, zero versus Gaussian padding, and dependence on expert-output weight. Appendix C adds an illustrative reasoning case study. The original insertion-depth analysis and Figure 5 are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five repetitions and reporting mean accuracy with standard deviation. No increased run count, new seed information, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedure is introduced. Additional result rows and their uncertainty values do not establish a changed statistical procedure.

E6.justification: v2 adds privacy-baseline curves, F1 scores, Adult and Llama-2 results, reasoning output, and component-ablation results. Original benchmark accuracy and efficiency values are retained. New findings include Adult accuracy of 76.08% for Llamdex versus 76.55% for Expert API, and Llama-2 Nursery accuracy of 31.89% versus 35.09% for Real Data LoRA. These are new comparisons, not improvements over v1 under identical settings.

T1.justification: Following Eq. (3), v1 states θ_Md ∩ θ_M = ∅, whereas v2 states θ_M ∩ θ_Ed = ∅. These constrain different parameter sets; the latter no longer expresses the stated separation between trainable parameters and the frozen LLM. The DP definition, Gaussian-mechanism theorem, and objectives otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The introduction changes the named target of the 'up to 26%' superiority claim from PATE-GAN to PromptPATE, while the abstract emphasizes state-of-the-art data synthesis. The central model-based knowledge-transfer contribution, privacy guarantees, 14% LoRA comparison, and inference-efficiency claim are retained.

C2.justification: Appendices C–D add localized interpretations: Adult's simpler schema explains API competitiveness, Bank's imbalance explains F1 behavior, Gaussian padding breaks parameter symmetry, and Llama-2 results indicate robustness to the base model. The earlier multi-task, complex-question, and multimodal limitations remain in Appendix E.

D1.justification: v2 supplies the exact answer-feedback template and follow-up prompt in Appendix C and Table 6. It also identifies Llama-2-7B and documents control settings for the new ablations. Existing optimizer settings, epoch counts, hardware, precision, and efficiency-evaluation sample budget remain unchanged.

R1.justification: PromptPATE through Duan et al. (2024) is newly cited; SeqPATE was already cited in v1. Other additions concern Adult, relational databases, F1, and Claude, while Song et al. (2024) is removed. The overall utility-versus-privacy taxonomy and model-based contribution positioning remain stable.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and several experimental passages are rewritten, alongside title and terminology changes. Dataset information, the evaluation example, training-efficiency discussion, insertion-layer analysis, and future-work discussion are reorganized into Appendices A–E. Section 5.3 and an impact statement are added, substantially changing the document structure.

P2.justification: v2 changes the publication template, expands Figure 2 into an architecture and training workflow, and redraws Figure 4 with additional curves and revised visual styling. Several existing displays move into appendices, while Tables 6–11 and Figures 6–7 add substantial new visual material. Figure 5 is reused unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added privacy comparators and component ablations strengthen evidence that was limited in v1, while Adult and F1 results reveal where Llamdex is competitive rather than uniformly superior. These benefits are tempered by unexplained uncertainty discrepancies between Tables 1 and 10, broad Llama-2 robustness wording despite LoRA winning on Nursery, and the non-equivalent parameter constraint introduced in Section 4. The net gain is useful but limited.
